summary: Practise emergency WASH assessment, water safety, sanitation planning, and response monitoring. Explore the 5-day course and outline.
lede: Humanitarian water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) training helps emergency response professionals assess needs and plan field services. Emergency WASH officers, programme coordinators and engineers practise needs assessment, water-supply planning and water-quality monitoring. They also develop sanitation and hygiene plans and use field data to track services and report response progress.
audienceIntro: This intermediate WASH humanitarian response course is designed for professionals who already work in emergency, public health, infrastructure, or humanitarian programme delivery and need to plan or monitor field services.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with humanitarian or emergency-response operations, public health, water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, or related field work. You should be comfortable reviewing basic service data and working with spreadsheets. No programming is required. Participants can complete the core exercises using supplied scenario information; access to Excel, KoboToolbox, or QGIS supports digital practice where available.
